in_text_mentions: Mammography showed an architectural distortion in the upper quadrants of the left breast, only clearly seen in the mediolateral oblique view (Figure 1). DBT—routinely performed at the patient's hospital—localized the lesion to the upper outer quadrant and further characterized it as a small irregular mass with long spicules (Figure 2). A targeted Ultrasound (US) showed a 10 mm solid nodule, with posterior acoustic shadowing (Figure 3). A tru-cut biopsy guided by US was performed, revealing a tubular carcinoma.

in_text_mentions: Mammography showed an architectural distortion in the upper quadrants of the left breast, only clearly seen in the mediolateral oblique view (Figure 1). DBT—routinely performed at the patient's hospital—localized the lesion to the upper outer quadrant and further characterized it as a small irregular mass with long spicules (Figure 2). A targeted Ultrasound (US) showed a 10 mm solid nodule, with posterior acoustic shadowing (Figure 3). A tru-cut biopsy guided by US was performed, revealing a tubular carcinoma.

in_text_mentions: as grade I, as well as all in situ malignant neoplastic tumors. For invasive malignant neoplastic tumors, 20 were grade I, six were grade II and seven were grade III. Among the 33 invasive malignant tumors, 19 were on the RMC (58%) from which 11 (33%) were classified as grade I, five (15%) as grade II tumors and three (9%) as grade III tumors, and 14 (42%) were on the LMC from which 11 (27%) were classified as grade I, five (3%) as grade II tumors and three (12%) as grade III tumors, as described in Table 4. Histological differences between tumors with different grades are showed in Figure 4.
